chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bishr narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Haytham narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath,
that whenever he would narrate to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), he would say: The best of the Ja'fars, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), narrated to me.

key_terms.حدثني: He narrated to me — indicating direct, personal transmission of hadith
key_terms.خير الجعافر: The best of the Ja'fars — an honorific title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing his superiority over all who bore the name Ja'far

ai.seo_question: How did Hafs ibn Ghiyath describe Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq when narrating hadith?
ai.summary: This narration records how Hafs ibn Ghiyath, a prominent Kufan qadi and narrator, expressed his deep reverence for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS). Whenever Hafs would transmit a hadith from the Imam, he would introduce him with the honorific title "the best of the Ja'fars" (khayr al-ja'afir), highlighting the Imam's distinguished status among all who bore the name Ja'far. This testimony is significant as Hafs was also a narrator for Sunni collections, making his praise of the sixth Imam a cross-sectarian acknowledgment of the Imam's scholarly eminence.
